content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sentiment turns negative or neutral (especially when sentiment drops below 0.00), leading to persistent lag in upward price movements.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85.00), model overreacts to recent highs and fails to adjust downward quickly — overshoots followed by underestimation of subsequent corrections.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.50), model tends to underestimate the true price rise, especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: it overcorrects downward after recent highs, failing to capture sustained upward momentum driven by positive sentiment.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows increasing underestimation as sentiment improves — model fails to fully account for sentiment-driven momentum in later days.
- When sentiment is low or negative, model ignores structural support levels and underestimates rebound potential — especially in the first 10 days of the forecast.
